findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
Observed no food handler’s licenses for the facility. All food handling employees should have a valid food handler’s licenses. Valid for 3 years. Employees should obtain a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas of the facility that are in need of repairs:
1. The floor to the right of the prep cooler was observed with damaged tiles.
2. The floor in front of the back door has similar damage observed (tiles), as well as behind the oven.

5. The wall by the back reach-in cooler/freezer has dry wall damage, as well as in the bathroom and next to the desk.

Discussed repairs with PIC. #1-4 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 12/19/22. Ensure repairs by next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and not use a clean barrier to turn off the faucet. Education conducted and hands rewashed to remedy the violation.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. 

On arrival the hand sink in the main prep area is observed with multiple rags stored in it. PIC was consulted and the rags removed during the inspection to correct the violation. Hand sinks should be only used for hand washing, not storage of old/used rags.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips

4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

On arrival as well as when foods had begun to be prepped, no sanitizers were available for use in the facility. Two sani buckets were made during the inspection using bleach to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

1) The floor to the right of the prep cooler is observed with multiple locations of damaged tiles allowing for rough surfaces that are not easily maintained clean. 2) the floor in front of the back door has similar damage observed. Repair prior to the next routine inspection. 3) The floor cover is missing for the drain to the left of the oven as well as the drain in front of the 3 part sink. Repair/replace and maintain functional grates.

6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. 

Floor coving is observed pulling away from the wall at multiple locations throughout the facility. Repair and maintain repaired moving foreword.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

On arrival, the PIC was unaware of any documentation to which employees had been informed of their reporting responsibilities in relation to symptoms or diseases related to food born illnesses. Enough SCDPH reporting agreements were given to the PIC during the inspection to cover all current employees and an extra for copies/ future employees. PIC is instructed to ensure that each employee signs an agreement prior to the follow up date.

findings.title: Hot food at proper temperatures
findings.comment:
Nacho cheese in the nacho cheese dispenser was not date marked. PIC stated the cheese had been in the dispenser for longer than seven days. Cheese was immediately discarded to CORRECT the violation.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed a container of pizza sauce left out at room temperature. When noted to staff and asked about their time marking policy, staff noted that the sauce was pulled out last night and used but then put back into refrigeration. When using time as a control for potentially hazardous foods, foods need to be discarded after the 4 hour mark. Do not put potentially hazardous foods requiring time as a control back into refrigeration. Sauce was discarded to correct the violation. 750-153(a) Food shall not be held more that 4 hours past the point it is removed from temperature control. Do not hold food in excess of four hours after removal from temperature control.
